findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the premise with pyproject.toml:239 (the `dev` extra already self-references `nava-rebar[agents,metrics]`): confirm whether `--extra dev` already provisions lizard and, if so, restate what changes #1/#2 actually accomplish (or drop them) and re-baseline AC line 1.
evidence: pyproject.toml:239 inside the `dev` extra: `"nava-rebar[agents,metrics]",` — with a comment (lines 235–238) stating it exists so the metrics stack RUNS in CI ('real polyglot lizard parsing')
pyproject.toml:178 `metrics = ["lizard>=1.23"]` is reached transitively by `--extra dev` via the self-reference

Plan Purpose: 'require three external tools that no bootstrap path installs'; item 1: '`uv sync --locked --extra dev` becomes `... --extra dev --extra metrics`. ... so worktree venvs are covered by the same change.'
findings.finding: The plan's central premise — that lizard is NOT installed by any bootstrap path and that adding `--extra metrics` is what will provision it — is refuted by the codebase: the `dev` extra self-references `nava-rebar[agents,metrics]`, so `uv sync --locked --extra dev` (and `pip install -e '.[dev]'`) already pull lizard transitively.
findings.location: 'What this ticket changes' items 1–2; Purpose ('no bootstrap path installs'); AC line 1
scenarios: A reviewer/implementer applies change #1 expecting it to newly enable lizard, when a fresh `make worktree` venv can already `import lizard` today
AC line 1 ('make install provisions lizard; a fresh make worktree venv can import lizard') is already satisfied on origin/main WITHOUT this ticket's change
findings.suggested_fix: Verify `uv sync --locked --extra dev` in a clean venv already yields `import lizard`; if it does, remove/replace the `--extra metrics` edits or re-scope the ticket to only the scc/jscpd documentation, and reword the Purpose/AC accordingly.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the plan with pyproject.toml:239's `nava-rebar[agents,metrics]` in the `dev` extra: verify on clean `main` whether `make install` already provisions lizard, then either re-scope item 1 (lizard is already covered — the net-new work is only scc/jscpd docs + install-unlocked parity) or state explicitly why the redundant `--extra metrics` is still wanted (e.g. decoupling from the self-referential dev extra), and make AC1 discriminate (assert the state changes, not that it merely holds).
evidence: pyproject.toml:239 `"nava-rebar[agents,metrics]"` inside the `dev` extra; the comment at 235-238 states it exists to 'Pull the agents and metrics stacks so optional-capability validation tests ... (and real polyglot lizard parsing) RUN in CI rather than skipping.'
Makefile:46 current `make install` is `uv sync --locked --extra dev` — which resolves `dev` and therefore `[metrics]`/lizard transitively.
Purpose claims lizard is among 'three external tools that no bootstrap path installs' — but the dev/CI bootstrap path already installs it via the self-referential extra.

`.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml:70` also uses `uv sync --locked --extra dev`, so CI already provisions lizard (AC5 'CI is unaffected' is true because metrics is already present, not because the change adds nothing observable).
findings.finding: The plan's premise and Change #1 do not account for the `dev` extra already pulling `[metrics]` (lizard) transitively, so the lizard portion of the change may be redundant and AC1 may already pass on `main`.
findings.location: Purpose + 'What this ticket changes' item 1 + AC1
scenarios: An implementer adds `--extra metrics`, runs AC1, sees `import lizard` succeed, and concludes the change fixed provisioning — when a fresh `main` `make install` already provisioned it, so the observation proves nothing about the diff.
Reviewers/operators read the Purpose's 'no bootstrap path installs' and mis-scope the follow-on scc bug work on a false premise.
findings.suggested_fix: Correct the Purpose to note lizard is ALREADY installed transitively by `--extra dev` (via the self-referential `nava-rebar[agents,metrics]`), so item 1's `--extra metrics` is explicit-not-transitive belt-and-suspenders rather than a fix; concentrate the ticket's net-new value on the scc/jscpd documentation + the `install-unlocked` `.[dev,metrics]` parity, and reword AC1 to something that actually discriminates.

evidence: 2 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State in item 3 that docs/local-dev-env.md should reuse the exact `brew install scc` and `npm install -g jscpd` commands from the Machine setup section (with version note) as the canonical instructions.
evidence: 'they need a documented install step -- docs/local-dev-env.md is the natural home' does not enumerate the commands to write.
Machine setup lists `brew install scc` and `npm install -g jscpd` but is framed as machine-specific reproducibility, not doc content.
findings.finding: AC3 requires docs/local-dev-env.md to 'document installing scc and jscpd' but the plan does not specify the exact install commands or version pins to put in the doc; the executor must infer them (the Machine setup section gives brew/npm/uv commands but does not designate them as the canonical doc content).
findings.location: 'What this ticket changes' item 3 and AC3
scenarios: Two executors write different install instructions (with/without version pins, brew vs binary download).

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a step naming how CI provisions its venv (does it call `make install`?) and the concrete command that proves AC5 (e.g. inspect the CI workflow file and confirm the metrics extra is either desired or excluded).
evidence: The three change items (Makefile install, install-unlocked, docs) never mention CI.
AC5 is a disjunction that requires determining whether CI is affected, but no described step establishes how CI provisions its venv.
findings.finding: Acceptance criterion 5 ('CI is unaffected, or the change to CI is explicit and justified') has no covering step in the 'What this ticket changes' section, and the plan never states whether CI invokes `make install` (which would now also install lizard) or a separate path, so the executor cannot know what to check.
scenarios: CI runs `make install` and now pulls lizard into the CI image, changing the CI environment unacknowledged.
Executor cannot prove 'CI unaffected' because the CI invocation path is undocumented.
findings.suggested_fix: State in the plan whether CI uses `make install`; if so, note that lizard becomes an additive CI dependency (harmless, scc/jscpd remain absent → Unavailable) and cite the CI config file to inspect as the proving artifact for AC5.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the title's 'run code-health metrics' claim with the body's admission that scc-backed size metrics remain non-functional — narrow the title/scope to the metrics actually enabled (complexity/duplication + toolchain provisioning) or explicitly note size metrics are out of scope pending the sibling bug.
evidence: Title: 'so every new project venv can run code-health metrics'
Body: 'The scc-backed size metrics do NOT -- see the sibling bug on the missing --by-file flag.'
AC set covers lizard import + Unavailable degradation, not end-to-end 'run code-health metrics'
findings.finding: The title promises 'every new project venv can run code-health metrics', but the body states the scc-backed size metrics do NOT return real values (blocked on a sibling bug), so post-change a venv still cannot run the full code-health metrics — only complexity/duplication. The end-state proof (ACs) verifies lizard import and Unavailable-degradation, not that the metrics command actually produces complete code-health output.
findings.location: Title vs. 'Machine setup' note: 'The scc-backed size metrics do NOT -- see the sibling bug on the missing --by-file flag.'
scenarios: A contributor reads the title, provisions a fresh venv, runs `rebar metrics` expecting full code-health output, and still sees size metrics reporting the broken/unavailable value.
findings.suggested_fix: Retitle to something like 'Provision the metrics analyzer toolchain by default (complexity/duplication now real; size metrics pending sibling scc fix)' or add an explicit scope note that full code-health output awaits the --by-file fix.
